payload.reasoning_summary: FASE-1 is the earliest incomplete phase. The accepted repository bootstrap leaves packages/core stubbed, and ADR-009 plus canonical encoding is an explicit prerequisite to StateHash and replay comparison. This is the smallest coherent current-phase unit and must precede dependent RNG, world, ledger, and replay work.
risks: An underspecified ADR could make persisted bytes implementation-dependent and force a breaking encoding-version migration.
Ambiguous unordered-collection or Unicode-key semantics could create cross-runtime replay divergence.
The previously stalled encoder task indicates delivery risk; keeping StateHash and unrelated core primitives out of scope is necessary to maintain reviewability.

acceptance_criteria: ADR-009 exists under docs/decisions and specifies enough byte-level detail, including type tags and framing, for an independent implementation to reproduce identical bytes.
The implementation contains no encoding decision absent from ADR-009; ADR-009 is committed in the same change before or with code depending on it.
Logically equal supported objects encode to byte-identical output regardless of property insertion order.
Object keys are ordered by their UTF-8 byte sequences using a locale-independent comparison; tests include keys for which locale or UTF-16 ordering would give a different result.
Safe integers use a type marker distinct from bigint; non-integer numbers and integers outside Number safe-integer bounds are rejected deterministically.
Bigints use the ADR-defined signed decimal ASCII representation with an explicit sign and cannot collide with safe-integer encodings.
undefined, NaN, positive and negative Infinity, and negative zero each produce an explicit deterministic error and are never normalized.
Ordered collections preserve element order; every supported unordered collection is canonicalized using the exact sorting rule recorded in ADR-009.
Changing encodingVersion changes the canonical byte sequence for the same supported value.
The encoder does not read time, randomness, locale, environment, filesystem, network, or mutable global state.
No StateHash API or finalTick-specific behavior is introduced by this change.
Repository lint, strict typecheck, dependency-boundary checks, and all pre-existing tests pass.
must_preserve: All accepted monorepo bootstrap tests and checks remain green.
Existing workspace and dependency boundaries remain unchanged.
Pure packages remain free of nondeterministic APIs and forbidden dependencies.
INV-22 requirement that equal logical states can yield equal canonical bytes; StateHash must later exclude finalTick outside this encoder.
task.objective: Specify and implement a versioned byte-level canonical encoding whose output depends only on the supported logical value and encodingVersion.
out_of_scope: StateHash implementation or finalTick filtering logic.
Positional RNG, branded domain numeric types, ledger, price generation, Electron scaffolding, UI, and installer work.
Support for types not explicitly admitted by ADR-009.
Changes to CICLO_SPEC.md, unrelated workspaces, or existing dependency-boundary architecture.
required_tests: Golden-vector tests asserting exact bytes for every supported primitive and container type, nesting, empty values, UTF-8 keys, integer boundaries, signed bigint values, and encodingVersion.
Permutation tests showing identical bytes for logically equal objects created with different insertion orders.
UTF-8 byte-order tests that would fail under localeCompare or UTF-16 code-unit sorting.
Rejection tests for undefined in every admitted position, NaN, both infinities, negative zero, fractional numbers, unsafe integers, unsupported values, and cyclic structures if containers can cycle.
Collision tests distinguishing safe integers from bigint and structurally different nested values.
Ordered-collection tests proving order affects bytes and unordered-collection tests proving insertion order does not affect bytes.
Run the repository test suite, lint, strict typecheck, and dependency-boundary validation.
scope: Write ADR-009 with an independently reproducible byte grammar, type markers, length framing, UTF-8 rules, object-key ordering, integer and bigint representations, collection semantics, prohibited values, and encodingVersion participation.
Implement CanonicalEncoder in packages/core for exactly the value types admitted by ADR-009.
Define deterministic, explicit error behavior for unsupported or prohibited inputs.
Export the encoder and its public error/types through the existing packages/core public entry point.
Add focused unit and determinism tests for the ADR-defined format.
task.title: Define ADR-009 and implement deterministic CanonicalEncoder
